query: How will advanced AI compute export controls be enforced?
response:
**Part 1:**  
They will be enforced by expanding existing controls on the export, reexport, and transfer (in‑country) of advanced computing ICs needed to build large training clusters and by imposing new controls on the export, reexport, and transfer (in‑country) of certain closed AI model weights.

**Part 2:**  
In practice, all exports of advanced AI chips will require licenses or exemptions, giving regulators leverage over where large compute clusters can be built and who can access them. Controls then extend to compute access, restricting which entities may use controlled chips for frontier model development. Finally, there are controls on the transfer and storage of controlled model weights, with stringent security and location requirements and access differentiated by country tiers and validated end users. Together, these measures govern diffusion along the entire AI compute supply chain, from chip production and data centers to model deployment.
